title: Automatic deletion of Pending account after 30 days
gherkin:
Feature: Pending Account Cleanup
  Scenario: System automatically deletes Pending account after 30 days
    Given a user account is in Pending status
    And the account was created 30 days ago
    When the cleanup job runs
    Then the account should be deleted from the system
    And the account should no longer be retrievable
rationale: Core requirement from PRIMARY evidence E1 and E4: System shall automatically delete any user account that remains in Pending status for more than 30 days. This is the primary functional requirement for R6.
usedContextItems: System shall automatically delete any user account that remains in Pending status for more than 30 days

Subject: Escalation: exception handling for priority customers

Hi Dev Team,

Support keeps running into cases where a high-priority customer wants to secure an item even though the system currently treats the time window as blocked because of another pending request.

Operationally, the team is asking whether specially authorized staff should be able to intervene in those cases and resolve the conflict manually, rather than forcing the customer to wait for the ordinary availability flow to clear on its own. In practice this would mean allowing a priority booking path to take precedence over weaker, not-yet-confirmed demand.

Please do not treat this as confirmed product policy yet. We need guidance on whether this should remain a support-side exception process, or whether the booking logic itself is expected to support it.

Regards,
Sarah (Support Lead)

Feature: Pending Account Lifecycle
  Scenario: Account transitions to Pending status after successful registration
    Given a user completes the registration form
    When registration is successful
    Then the account status should be set to Pending
    And the account should not be verified
rationale: Operative context establishes that Pending status is set upon successful registration before email verification. This is a prerequisite state for the cleanup requirement.
usedContextItems: System shall set the account status to Pending upon successful registration and before email verification

Subject: Escalation: exception handling for priority customers

Hi Dev Team,

Support keeps running into cases where a high-priority customer wants to secure an item even though the system currently treats the time window as blocked because of another pending request.

Operationally, the team is asking whether specially authorized staff should be able to intervene in those cases and resolve the conflict manually, rather than forcing the customer to wait for the ordinary availability flow to clear on its own. In practice this would mean allowing a priority booking path to take precedence over weaker, not-yet-confirmed demand.

Please do not treat this as confirmed product policy yet. We need guidance on whether this should remain a support-side exception process, or whether the booking logic itself is expected to support it.

Regards,
Sarah (Support Lead)

Feature: Account Status Transitions
  Scenario: Status change to Pending takes effect immediately
    Given a user completes registration
    When the system sets the account status to Pending
    Then the status change should be reflected immediately
    And no delay should occur before the new status is active
rationale: Operative context specifies that account status changes take effect immediately, ensuring that Pending status is active without delay for cleanup tracking purposes.
usedContextItems: Account status changes take effect immediately

Subject: Escalation: exception handling for priority customers

Hi Dev Team,

Support keeps running into cases where a high-priority customer wants to secure an item even though the system currently treats the time window as blocked because of another pending request.

Operationally, the team is asking whether specially authorized staff should be able to intervene in those cases and resolve the conflict manually, rather than forcing the customer to wait for the ordinary availability flow to clear on its own. In practice this would mean allowing a priority booking path to take precedence over weaker, not-yet-confirmed demand.

Please do not treat this as confirmed product policy yet. We need guidance on whether this should remain a support-side exception process, or whether the booking logic itself is expected to support it.

Regards,
Sarah (Support Lead)

Feature: Data Minimization on Cleanup
  Scenario: Associated personal data is removed upon automatic deletion
    Given a Pending account is scheduled for automatic deletion
    When the cleanup job executes
    Then all associated personal data should be removed
    And only minimal audit logs required by retention policy should remain
rationale: Operative context indicates that all associated personal data must be removed upon automatic deletion, except for minimal audit logs required by retention policy. This ensures GDPR data minimization compliance.
usedContextItems: All associated personal data must be removed upon automatic deletion, except for minimal audit logs required by retention policy

Subject: Escalation: exception handling for priority customers

Hi Dev Team,

Support keeps running into cases where a high-priority customer wants to secure an item even though the system currently treats the time window as blocked because of another pending request.

Operationally, the team is asking whether specially authorized staff should be able to intervene in those cases and resolve the conflict manually, rather than forcing the customer to wait for the ordinary availability flow to clear on its own. In practice this would mean allowing a priority booking path to take precedence over weaker, not-yet-confirmed demand.

Please do not treat this as confirmed product policy yet. We need guidance on whether this should remain a support-side exception process, or whether the booking logic itself is expected to support it.

Regards,
Sarah (Support Lead)

Feature: Pending Account Access Control
  Scenario: Pending account cannot authenticate to the platform
    Given a user account is in Pending status
    When the user attempts to authenticate
    Then authentication should fail
    And access to the platform should be denied
rationale: Operative context establishes that Pending accounts cannot authenticate or access the platform, which is a key characteristic of the Pending state that precedes cleanup.
usedContextItems: Pending accounts cannot authenticate or access the platform

Date: 2026-02-24 15:30
Subject: Escalation: exception handling for priority customers

Hi Dev Team,

Support keeps running into cases where a high-priority customer wants to secure an item even though the system currently treats the time window as blocked because of another pending request.

Operationally, the team is asking whether specially authorized staff should be able to intervene in those cases and resolve the conflict manually, rather than forcing the customer to wait for the ordinary availability flow to clear on its own. In practice this would mean allowing a priority booking path to take precedence over weaker, not-yet-confirmed demand.

Please do not treat this as confirmed product policy yet. We need guidance on whether this should remain a support-side exception process, or whether the booking logic itself is expected to support it.

Regards,
Sarah (Support Lead)

Feature: Pending Account Cleanup Timing
  Scenario: Account is not deleted before 30-day threshold
    Given a user account is in Pending status
    And the account was created 29 days ago
    When the cleanup job runs
    Then the account should not be deleted
    And the account should remain in Pending status
rationale: Clarifies the boundary condition of the 30-day requirement. Accounts should only be deleted after more than 30 days, not before. This ensures users have the full grace period.
usedContextItems: System shall automatically delete any user account that remains in Pending status for more than 30 days

Subject: Escalation: exception handling for priority customers

Hi Dev Team,

Support keeps running into cases where a high-priority customer wants to secure an item even though the system currently treats the time window as blocked because of another pending request.

Operationally, the team is asking whether specially authorized staff should be able to intervene in those cases and resolve the conflict manually, rather than forcing the customer to wait for the ordinary availability flow to clear on its own. In practice this would mean allowing a priority booking path to take precedence over weaker, not-yet-confirmed demand.

Please do not treat this as confirmed product policy yet. We need guidance on whether this should remain a support-side exception process, or whether the booking logic itself is expected to support it.

Regards,
Sarah (Support Lead)

Feature: Manual Account Deletion Exception
  Scenario: Manual account deletion triggers 14-day recovery grace period
    Given an administrator initiates manual deletion of a Pending account
    When the deletion is processed
    Then the account should enter a grace period state
    And the account should be recoverable for 14 days
    And after 14 days the account should be permanently wiped
rationale: Exception from operative context: Manual account deletion may require a 14-day grace period for recovery before permanent wipe (unconfirmed). This is an exception scenario that differs from automatic cleanup and should be tested separately.
usedContextItems: Manual account deletion may require a 14-day grace period for recovery before permanent wipe (unconfirmed)

Subject: Escalation: exception handling for priority customers

Hi Dev Team,

Support keeps running into cases where a high-priority customer wants to secure an item even though the system currently treats the time window as blocked because of another pending request.

Operationally, the team is asking whether specially authorized staff should be able to intervene in those cases and resolve the conflict manually, rather than forcing the customer to wait for the ordinary availability flow to clear on its own. In practice this would mean allowing a priority booking path to take precedence over weaker, not-yet-confirmed demand.

Please do not treat this as confirmed product policy yet. We need guidance on whether this should remain a support-side exception process, or whether the booking logic itself is expected to support it.

Regards,
Sarah (Support Lead)
